cards.text: Through Haggai the prophet, the LORD told Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, Joshua, the high priest, and the people that His house lies in ruins while each of them is busy with his own house (Haggai 1:1, 4, 9). He even said He had summoned a drought (Haggai 1:11). Now Zerubbabel, Joshua and all the remnant of the people have heard that whole message.

cards.question: Zerubbabel, Joshua and all the remnant of the people have heard the LORD's message through Haggai. What do they do with it?

answers.text: They obey the voice of the LORD
They return to their own houses
They wait until the time has come

cards.question: The leaders and the people obey the words of the prophet Haggai, because the LORD their God had ___ him.

cards.text: So the people feared the LORD. Then Haggai, the messenger of the LORD, brings them a new message from the LORD.

cards.question: Haggai brings a short new message from the LORD to the people who just obeyed. What does the LORD say?

cards.text: Then something happens inside Zerubbabel, the governor. His spirit gets stirred up, like dough that finally starts to rise after you've been staring at it for an hour.

cards.question: Somebody stirs the spirit of Zerubbabel, the governor. Who is it?
The LORD stirs the spirit of Zerubbabel the governor, but not the spirits of the rest of the people.

cards.text: Joshua the high priest and all the remnant of the people get their spirits stirred too. And nobody schedules a meeting to plan the next meeting. They COME.

cards.question: Their spirits stirred, the people come and ___ the work on the house of the LORD of Hosts, their God.

cards.text: And the start date gets written down: the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month, in the second year of the king. Friend, if my bakery ever got a day like that, I'd tape it to the oven door and point at it with my mustache every morning.

cards.question: The work on the house of the LORD begins in the second year of a king. Which king is it?
